title: Mini Eval Proxy Workbench — personal scratchpad
content:
Goal:
Quick personal notes for a tiny evaluation proxy that we can ship in Private/Dedicated as a low-risk quality gate and local sampling harness. Not a full Redwood Optimize integration yet — think 'mini-eval' as an embeddable microservice that runs small prompt suites, computes a handful of quality signals, and surfaces regressions with minimal telemetry and cost.

Why: (motivation)
- customers want lightweight local regression checks before switching model pins (esp. Private).
- full Optimize is heavy; a tiny proxy reduces friction for SRE/SE to run smoke-evals on rollout.
- helpful for devs to run quick A/B checks without provisioning large infra.

High-level sketch (API + behaviour):
- proxy runs alongside runtime (sidecar or small HTTP service).
- accepts a bundle: {candidate_model, baseline_model?, prompt_set_id, eval_config} (see below).
- executes up to N short prompts (configurable), collects outputs, computes metrics (exact-match-ish, BLEU-ish, tok-overlap, hallucination heuristics, latency, token-usage).
- returns {report_id, summary: {pass:bool, fail_reasons:[], scores:...}, raw_samples:[] } and stores detailed artifact to local disk or S3 depending on deployment flags.
- supports a 'fast-only' mode that runs syntactic/cheap checks for tight rollouts.

API shape draft (HTTP/JSON):
POST /v1/mini-eval/run
body: {
  "candidate": {"model":"m:x:123","variant":"q4o"},
  "baseline": {"model":"m:x:120"}, // optional
  "prompts": ["prompt-id-1","prompt-id-2"] or inline prompts
  "eval_config": {"max_tokens":64, "sample_seeds":[42,99], "metrics":["tok_overlap","assertion_check","latency_p50"], "parallelism":4, "timeout_ms":8000},
  "artifact_destination": "local|s3|none"
}
response: {"report_id":"meval-20250110-xyz","summary":{...},"status":"queued|running|done|error"}

GET /v1/mini-eval/report/{report_id} -> full report JSON or compact summary
POST /v1/mini-eval/prompts/upload -> small prompt sets (csv/json)

Config file prototype (YAML-like but represented as JSON here):
- default.max_prompts = 20
- default.parallel = 2
- cheap_checks.threshold = 0.75 // threshold for fast pass recommendation
- retention: local_days:14, s3_bucket: "redwood-mini-eval-artifacts"
- secrets: use KMS for S3 creds in Private

Metrics to compute (minimal):
1) token_overlap: proportion of shared token substrings between baseline and candidate (fast, cheap)
2) generation_drift_score: normalized edit distance between baseline and candidate summaries
3) assertion_check: regex/assertion-based pass/fail on structured outputs (useful for function-calling checks)
4) latency_p50/p95: measure model response times (compute environ-adjusted)
5) hallucination_signal: heuristic fingerprint (named-entity hallucination count vs. seed corpus)
6) cost_estimate_tokens: rough token cost delta

Local artifact format:
- report.json (summary + per-prompt entries)
- samples.csv (prompt, baseline_output, candidate_output, metrics)
- quick_png.png (tiny histograms)

Integration points:
- Redwood Console: we expose a webhook to push compact report summaries to per-tenant console if allowed.
- Optimize: eventually we can export reports into Optimize's eval storage (one-time mapping).
- CI/Deployment: a post-deploy hook can trigger mini-eval for canary iterations.

Operational constraints / safety:
- must not send any PII off-prem by default in Private deployments. Default = local only.
- artifact encryption at rest (use KMS/HSM where available).
- small CPU/GPU footprint: prefer synchronous calls to existing inference runtime rather than a separate GPU pool.

Implementation notes / fast prototypes:
- implement as tiny Go binary that calls Redwood runtime via internal SDK (reuse token exchange).
- use an internal mini-eval DSL for assertions (like: assert(cols.price > 0) or contains(entity:org)).
- cache prompt-level tokenization to avoid double-tokenizing on repeated runs.
- embed a tiny JS runner for assertion sandboxing (restrict to whitelisted ops).

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Q: minimal set of metrics that are informative and low-cost? Need quick validation with a few real tenant prompt-sets.
- Q: how do we represent 'baseline equivalence' vs 'better/worse' for subjective tasks? Add manual review flag?
- Q: UX in Console: inline 'eval' button on model-pin page vs separate mini-eval tab?
- TODO: mock up a simple HTML report with diffs + token-cost delta (Jamal to help).
- TODO: wire a tiny SLO check that flags if latency_p95 > model_slo*1.5
- TODO: small integration test that runs in Private on local docker: spin up runtime (dev image) + mini-eval sidecar run a 10-prompt test.

Quick experiment plan (week-by-week):
- Week 0: local PoC that hits hosted runtime with 5 prompts, 2 samples each, compute token_overlap and latency.
- Week 1: hook basic artifact save and a GET report endpoint. Add small CLI.
- Week 2: run against 3 internal model variants, collect manual labels for correlation with metrics.
- Week 3: iterate metrics (drop noisy ones), add 'fast-only' mode.

Notes to self (shorthand):
- keep config surface tiny; team will want more knobs later but start opinionated.
- default retention short to avoid storage costs in test clusters.
- name: "mini-eval-proxy" (working name, ok to rename to eval-sentinel later)

References / links:
- Slack: #eng-mini-eval (placeholder)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-1212
- GH sketch: gh.com/redwood/mini-eval-proxy (private)

Random scribbles:
- think about a 'sanity-only' profile for canary (run 3 synthetic checks only).
- maybe a CLI flag --no-network for truly local-only runs.

End of scratchpad.

(MT)
